title: modern gurus and their cautions (Keeper-framed)
hook: a line of people, hands on shoulders, sure of the way. none of them can see
tomorrow: is a hard question for a teacher doubt, or respect?

segments.voice: Yesterday, modern gurus and their cautions began with the word itself: gu, darkness, ru, what removes it. Today, the oldest caution, and a look back at the week.
screen: `HONOR THE LAMP. LOOK AT THE LIGHT.`

segments.voice: On a trail you've never walked, it's easy to just follow the person in front and trust they know the way. An old Upanishad draws a line like that. People walk down a road, each with a hand on the shoulder of the one ahead. They move with confidence. They're sure of the way. Not one of them can see, and that includes the one at the front.
screen: `FOLLOW THE PERSON IN FRONT.` → `HANDS ON SHOULDERS, SURE OF THE WAY.` → `NOBODY CAN SEE.`

segments.voice: The Mundaka Upanishad says it in paraphrase: people living in ignorance, wise in their own eyes, puffed up with learning, wander round and round, like the blind led by the blind. A few verses later comes the remedy. A seeker who wants to know the truth should go, fuel in hand, to a teacher who is two things: shrotriya, learned in the Veda, and brahmanishtha, established in Brahman, settled in the reality the texts point to. The fuel was the student's humble gift, sticks for the teacher's sacred fire. The two marks belong together. Learning alone can be the one at the front of the line, quoting beautifully and seeing nothing. Notice what's missing from the list: a large following, a famous name, a striking personality. A crowd can walk in a line too. Now hold the week up. A room that sings the names back. A nickname from a song. A door that opens on devotion. Grass, and a tree that gives shade. A plate that stops at the altar. A word that means the remover of darkness. And a line of the blind, with a test that's quiet and hard to fake.
screen: `THE BLIND LED BY THE BLIND.` · `FUEL IN HAND.` · `LEARNED, AND ROOTED.` · `A WEEK OF THE NAMES, AND A TEST.` · then, large: `LEARNED, AND ROOTED, BOTH AT ONCE.`

segments.voice: If you can, stand and walk slowly across the room and back, eyes open, noticing each thing you'd miss if you were only following someone's shoulder. If walking isn't possible right now, rest your open hands in your lap as if carrying a small bundle of sticks, the student's gift, and breathe.
Modern gurus and their cautions: today, two marks of a real teacher, and a road full of the blind.
screen: `MODERN GURUS AND THEIR CAUTIONS — today's word`.

segments.voice: Last line of the week, from modern gurus and their cautions: learned, and rooted, both at once. That's the week.

fork.setup: a friend quotes scripture perfectly, every time, but he's cruel to his little sister. by the Mundaka's two marks, what's missing?

fork.reveal: shrotriya and brahmanishtha: learned, and established in what the texts point to. learning alone can be the one at the front of the line, quoting beautifully and seeing nothing.

chat.meaning: The Mundaka's test is shrotriya and brahmanishtha, learned and rooted. A big following isn't on its list; a crowd can walk in a line too.
